title: The entire Asset Liability Management enforcement layer is unbuilt: detection and reporting substitute for penalties
content:
Three provisions in the same Section leave the framework without teeth. A.3.3.2.2.2: "In the near term there will be no penalties for Prime Agents for failing to maintain the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral." A.3.3.2.3.2: DAB penalties "will be specified in a future iteration." A.3.3.2.4.3: penalties for failing Peg Defense obligations likewise "will be specified in a future iteration."

What exists instead is visibility. A.3.3.2.2.2.1 requires the Core Council Risk Advisor to build a tool that automatically detects and reports failures, with each violation reported within 24 hours to five parties: the Core Facilitator, Core GovOps, the Agent's Operational Facilitator, its Operational GovOps, and the Agent itself.

So compliance currently rests on three things: the ASC Incentive making compliance economically neutral rather than costly, reputational exposure through multi-party reporting, and the general remedies available elsewhere (Core GovOps' power to restrict Allocation System usage). This is a reasonable interim design — the incentive removes the motive to under-hold, so detection may be sufficient — but it means the 5% minimum is currently a monitored target rather than an enforced floor, exactly as the Risk Capital penalties are in shadow mode (A.3.2.2.7.2.1.1.7).

A.3.3.2.2.3 goes further and suspends the requirement itself for one Agent: "due to limitations in the infrastructure on Solana, Keel is exempt from the requirement to maintain the Minimum Actively Stabilizing Collateral," with removal promised in a future iteration.

That exemption is worth noting on its own terms. A per-Agent ratio guarantees the aggregate only if every Agent complies (A.3.3.1.3); one exempt Agent breaks the derivation, so Sky's system-wide ASC coverage is now below 5% of the Collateral Portfolio by exactly Keel's share. A technical limitation on one chain has been converted directly into a reduction in the ecosystem's peg-defense capacity, with no compensating requirement imposed elsewhere.
description: No penalties exist for missing the ASC minimum, DAB and Peg Defense penalties are deferred to a future iteration, and Keel is exempt outright due to Solana infrastructure limits.
